From abbd00b82a2771b0460ba2cffdb1343aa827ccde Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Nov 2011 14:30:05 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] net/can/mscan: Fix buggy listen only mode setting

This patch fixes an issue introduced recently with commit
452448f9283e1939408b397e87974a418825b0a8.

CC: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c b/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
index 74f3b1829e02..1c82dd8b896e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
+++ b/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
@@ -581,7 +581,7 @@ static int mscan_open(struct net_device *dev)
 
 	priv->open_time = jiffies;
 
-	if (ctrlmode.flags & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
+	if (priv->can.ctrlmode & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
 		setbits8(&regs->canctl1, MSCAN_LISTEN);
 	else
 		clrbits8(&regs->canctl1, MSCAN_LISTEN);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c`**
- The condition for setting the listen-only mode has been modified. 
- The original line checked `ctrlmode.flags` for the `CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY` flag, while the updated line checks `priv->can.ctrlmode` for the same flag.
- This change ensures that the listen-only mode is set correctly based on the current control mode of the device.

### Relationships
- The modification in `mscan.c` directly addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified by its hash) that incorrectly handled the listen-only mode setting. 
- By changing the condition to reference `priv->can.ctrlmode`, the patch corrects the logic to ensure that the listen-only mode is accurately determined based on the device's current state, thereby fixing the bug.

```c
if (ctrlmode.flags & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
```
Reason:
This line incorrectly references `ctrlmode.flags` instead of `priv->can.ctrlmode`, which means the condition to check if the device should enter listen-only mode is based on an incorrect variable. As a result, the device may not enter listen-only mode when it should, leading to improper behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (priv->can.ctrlmode & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
```
Reason:
This line correctly references `priv->can.ctrlmode`, ensuring that the condition checks the actual control mode of the device. By using the correct variable, the device can now properly enter listen-only mode when required, fixing the bug introduced in the previous commit.
